title: Patch flatness + side-count stop criterion replaces MAX_PATCH_VERTS
description:
Today SemanticPatchDecomposer splits any final patch that exceeds MAX_PATCH_VERTS (2500) via positional k-means. This is a vertex-count heuristic, not a geometric-quality heuristic: a patch with 2000 verts that's highly curved and 12-sided is treated as 'done' (no split), while a flat 4-sided patch with 2600 verts gets split for no good reason.

Replace MAX_PATCH_VERTS with a composite 'needs further subdivision' criterion:
1. Curvature variance: stddev of per-vertex curvature across the patch. Low = flat = keep. High = bumpy = split.
2. Boundary 'side count': count corner vertices on the patch boundary — vertices where boundary dihedral (or boundary direction) changes by > threshold. A patch with 4 corners is already well-suited to Coons representation; 5+ means a split could simplify.
3. Aspect ratio: patches with area-to-perimeter² ratios far from 1:4π are elongated or concave and likely want further splitting.

A patch is 'done' (no further split) when: side_count ≈ 4 AND curvature_variance < T_FLAT AND aspect_ratio is reasonable. Otherwise split with k informed by the dominant deviation.

Motivation: from the PATCH-1+2 follow-up — 'obviously you could technically make a mesh from just two patches if you have N-sided patches but that wouldn't be simplifying the mesh'. The stopping rule should reward patches that actually look like Coons-patch candidates.
definition-of-done: Composite quality score replaces the MAX_PATCH_VERTS branch in SemanticPatchDecomposer. Validated on skull and one other reference that the patch count tracks complexity rather than raw vertex density.
testing-plan: Run on the skull and a simpler organic reference (hand or tube). Compare patch counts vs. visible complexity. A smooth tube should produce 4-6 patches; the skull should not balloon.
